title: the Marlowe Estate Rising
premise: Estate lawyer Ulyana Quintana, who has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental, is summoned to read the will of the late patriarch of Marlowe Estate—a will that legally cannot exist, dated after his confirmed death. When a body appears on the grounds dressed in clothes stolen from Ulyana's own closet, they realize someone is framing them and forcing them out of the shadows. The victim turns out to be connected to the one case everyone swore was closed: the death of Marlowe's daughter ten years ago, ruled a suicide by the very detective now hunting Ulyana. As the estate's found family of servants, heirs, and hangers-on splinters between loyalty and truth, Ulyana must expose a conspiracy reaching into the local police force before the killer completes the frame. In the end, Ulyana chooses truth over safety, delivering evidence that convicts the true killer—the patriarch himself, whose 'death' was staged—while finding a real home among the people they once merely observed.
about_author: Jonah Eriksen is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade reading other people's final wishes in small-town courthouses. They write mysteries about the quiet people who notice everything, and live off-grid with two judgmental cats.

chapters.title: The Will That Couldn't Be
chapters.summary: Ulyana Quintana arrives at fog-shrouded Marlowe Estate to read a will dated three days after its maker's confirmed death. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination as the document's impossible date suggests the dead man may not be dead.

chapters.title: Heirs and Strangers
chapters.summary: Ulyana meets the household: the bitter eldest son, the devoted housekeeper, a young groundskeeper with no surname, and a niece nobody invited. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: wary observation; Ulyana catalogs secrets like inventory, keeping their usual distance.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: The groundskeeper finds a corpse in the greenhouse wearing Ulyana's own missing coat and scarf. POV: alternating Ulyana and Detective Sorrel Vance, who once closed the case Ulyana solved quietly. Emotional beat: terror—the invisible observer is now the center of the story.

chapters.title: What the Police Remember
chapters.summary: Vance interrogates Ulyana, revealing she knows about the three 'accidents' Ulyana solved off the record—and resents it. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: antagonism with an undercurrent of grudging respect; both are hunters who hate being hunted.

chapters.title: The Closed Case
chapters.summary: Ulyana digs into the file everyone swears is shut: the daughter's suicide ten years ago, signed off personally by Vance's mentor. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread and resolve—the new murder is a message tied to the old one.

chapters.title: Closet Confessions
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces the stolen clothes through the house and discovers someone had access to their guest room for weeks. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: violated intimacy; for the first time, invisibility feels like vulnerability rather than armor.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Silence
chapters.summary: Mrs. Adeyemi, the housekeeper, almost tells Ulyana something about the night the daughter died, then goes silent after a phone call. POV: Mrs. Adeyemi. Emotional beat: loyalty at war with conscience—she owes the family her whole life.

chapters.title: Second Funeral
chapters.summary: At the patriarch's memorial, Ulyana notices the casket was sealed by family request and the coroner's signature looks wrong. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the first domino of the old cover-up comes into view.

chapters.title: An Ally With a Record
chapters.summary: Vance, stonewalled by her own department, makes an uneasy offer: share what you find, stay out of my crime scenes. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; justice outside the law meets justice inside a broken system.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper's Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana learns the young groundskeeper is the daughter's secret child, hidden in plain sight for a decade. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through professionalism—the found family theme takes root.

chapters.title: Threats in Probate Language
chapters.summary: A legal notice threatens Ulyana's license unless they leave the estate; the letterhead belongs to a firm tied to the coroner. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: fear weaponized into stubbornness—they will not be driven off.

chapters.title: Fire in the Records Room
chapters.summary: The county archive holding the daughter's autopsy burns overnight; Ulyana had requested copies hours earlier. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: fury and guilt—someone inside the system is erasing the past in real time.

chapters.title: What Mrs. Adeyemi Buried
chapters.summary: The housekeeper finally speaks: she saw the patriarch alive weeks after his supposed death and was paid to forget. POV: Mrs. Adeyemi. Emotional beat: confession as liberation; loyalty to a dead man breaks against loyalty to the living boy.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Ulyana finds the real will hidden in the daughter's old music box, naming the groundskeeper sole heir and accusing his grandfather of murder. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by horror—the document is also a target on the boy's back.

chapters.title: Framed
chapters.summary: Police find the second will planted in Ulyana's car along with the victim's bloodstained cufflink. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: betrayal and panic—the frame tightens; Ulyana becomes fugitive and investigator at once.

chapters.title: The Household Divides
chapters.summary: The son wants Ulyana gone, the niece wants the truth, and the groundskeeper runs rather than be used as bait. POV: rotating household members. Emotional beat: the found family fractures under pressure, each choosing loyalty or truth.

chapters.title: Vance's Mentor
chapters.summary: Vance confronts her retired mentor, who admits signing the false autopsy but claims he was protecting the town from scandal—not the killer. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: disillusionment; her faith in the badge dies so justice can be born.

chapters.title: Night at the Mausoleum
chapters.summary: Following the will's cryptic reference, Ulyana opens the family mausoleum and finds the patriarch's coffin empty except for a recorder documenting his own crimes. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: vertigo—the dead man orchestrated everything, including his own legend.

chapters.title: The Living Dead Man
chapters.summary: The patriarch reveals himself alive, having faked death to test which heir would kill for the estate; he murdered the greenhouse victim to frame Ulyana and silence the housekeeper. POV: patriarch, then Ulyana. Emotional beat: icy confrontation—he offers Ulyana partnership in impunity.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: The household, tipped by the groundskeeper, converges on the estate to protect him; the son chooses truth over inheritance at last. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: the found family reassembles around the boy, choosing each other over blood and money.

chapters.title: Marlowe Estate Rising
chapters.summary: Climax: the patriarch tries to burn the estate and the second will together; Ulyana, Vance, and the household corner him, and he confesses on the recovered recorder before Vance arrests him for murders spanning a decade. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: catharsis—justice achieved by law and loyalty working together.

chapters.title: Probate, Finally
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ulyana reads the true will aloud, the groundskeeper inherits, and the household chooses to keep the estate as a shared home—with Ulyana, no longer invisible, staying for dinner. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: quiet belonging; the observer finally joins the picture.
